heading: Build and deploy
body:
By default, `ty bundle` writes `dist/web`. To check a release, use `--target all`. Then preview or package the single target that you plan to release. On the server, `ty start` serves the bundle and never builds it. `ty serve` also builds and watches, unless `NODE_ENV=production` is set: then it does neither.

A build compiles the services of different languages at the same time. `TAC_BUILD_JOBS` sets how many toolchains run at once; the default is the number of CPU cores divided by 3, from 1 to 4. Set it to 1 on a small machine or a CI runner with little memory. When `ty preview` or `ty serve` starts again, it serves the last build at once and builds again in the background.

Yon compiles each Kotlin, Rust, Dart, Go and Groovy handler once. The project keeps the result in `.tachyon/handlers`, and ty keeps a copy in `TAC_CACHE_DIR/runtime/handlers-v1` (the newest 512 copies), so another project or a fresh checkout with the same handler, models and compiler reuses it instead of compiling again. `ty cache clean` removes these copies.

The Tachyon cache is `~/Library/Caches/Tachyon` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Tachyon\Cache` on Windows and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tachyon` (or `~/.cache/tachyon`) on Linux. `TAC_CACHE_DIR` chooses another folder, and `ty cache status` prints the one in use with its per-language build caches (`dotnet-web`, `go-wasm`, `swift-wasm`, `kotlin-wasm`, `java-wasm`, `rust-wasm`, `dart-wasm`, `ruby-web`, `lua-web`, `cpp-wasm` and `typescript`). `ty cache clean` removes those build caches with the runtime cache; installed tools in the cache, such as the Pyodide files and TeaVM, stay. The cached web builds and handlers in this folder run in the browser and on the server, so anyone who can write to it can change your app. Keep it private to your own user account, and never share it between users. A copy is trusted by its name; `ty cache clean` repairs a damaged one (ADR 0037).

A native build writes the time from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and the commit from `GITHUB_SHA` into its build information. Without them it writes 0 and a commit of zeros, so the build information never depends on the clock.

`ty bundle --target windows --arch arm64` and `--arch x64` select the Windows architecture. Without `--arch`, an ARM64 build machine selects ARM64 and other machines select x64; `--arch native` uses that default. The choice sets the Rust companion target, WebView2 loader folder, C# runtime identifier and linker machine together. Build in a matching MSVC developer prompt: an ARM64 machine uses `vcvarsall.bat arm64` for ARM64 or `vcvarsall.bat arm64_amd64` for x64. A conflicting `VSCMD_ARG_TGT_ARCH` stops the build (`TY1605`), and `--arch` without a Windows target is refused (`TY1001`). Both architectures have bundle and helper execution evidence; WebView2 page rendering and interaction still need an interactive desktop qualification run.
